title: Studying Scripture
definition: Studying Scripture is the faithful practice of reading, observing, interpreting, and applying the written Word of God with reverence, humility, prayer, and obedience.
summary: God gave Scripture so His people may know Him, trust His promises, discern truth, and be equipped for faithful living.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the center and fulfillment of Scripture, and faithful study should lead the heart to behold Him, trust the Gospel, and follow Him in obedience.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Studying Scripture begins with the conviction that God has spoken. The Bible is not merely a religious book to sample when convenient; it is the Word of God to be received, understood, believed, and obeyed.

Bible study should be careful but not cold. It involves observation, interpretation, and application, but it must remain prayerful and humble.

Studying Scripture strengthens discernment, deepens worship, equips for service, exposes sin, comforts the suffering, and trains believers for discipleship.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Without regular Scripture study, believers become more vulnerable to error, discouragement, shallow thinking, and spiritual drift. Studying Scripture roots the heart in God's truth instead of personal emotion, cultural pressure, or secondhand faith.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Set aside time to read Scripture carefully and prayerfully. Ask what the text says, what it means, how it points to Christ, and how you should respond.
